ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the picture there is a polyline outline similar to a mountain peak, and it together with the horizontal line segment at the bottom encloses a hexagonal region. The six marked angles are respectively located at: the left bottom end, the upper-left peak, the middle concave turning point, the highest peak, the right-side turning point, and the right bottom end. The marked angles at the four non-bottom vertices are all drawn outside the hexagon and are exterior angles around those points; the marked angles at the two bottom endpoints are above the horizontal bottom side and outside the hexagon, and are exterior angles when forming a straight line with the bottom side. Reasoning: Regard the mountain-shaped outline together with the horizontal line segment at the bottom as a hexagon. Let the sum of the six interior angles of the hexagon be S. The sum of the interior angles of a hexagon is (6-2)×180°=720°. Each of the marked angles at the four non-bottom vertices equals 360° minus the corresponding interior angle; each of the marked angles at the two bottom endpoints equals 180° minus the corresponding interior angle. Therefore the sum of the six marked angles is 4×360°+2×180°-720°=1440°+360°-720°=1080°.

raw_record.question_text: What is the sum of the six marked angles in the picture?

method.method_draft: Treat the outline of the mountain-shaped figure together with the horizontal bottom segment as a 6-vertex polygon. Label its interior angles at the two bottom endpoints and the four upper/kink vertices. From the image, the marked angle at each of the four non-bottom vertices is the angle around the point outside the polygon, so it is 360° minus that polygon interior angle; at the two bottom endpoints, the marked angle lies above the straight base line outside the polygon, so it is 180° minus the corresponding interior angle. Since the interior angle sum of a hexagon is (6-2)·180° = 720°, the sum of the six marked angles is 4·360° + 2·180° - 720° = 1080°.
